tutorial.title: Discovering Types
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn about the different types of values we can store in variables.

lessons.title: Types
lessons.interactiveContent: We've already seen and used a lot of different kinds of values. In programming lingo, these different kind of values are called types.

lessons.title: Strings
lessons.interactiveContent:
Strings are characters between quotes " ", like the value "Cookies".

Make sure to pick "Cookies".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Strings are characters between quotes " ", like the value "Cookies". Store the dessert name so the program prints Cookies.

Make sure to pick dessert, followed by "Cookies".

lessons.title: Numbers
lessons.interactiveContent:
Number is another type we've already used. It represents numerical values like 42.

Make sure to pick 42.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Number is another type we've already used. It represents numerical values like 42. Store the score that prints 42.

Make sure to pick score, followed by 42.

lessons.title: Booleans
lessons.interactiveContent:
The type boolean contains only two values: the special values true and false.

Make sure to pick true.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The type boolean contains only two values: the special values true and false.

Set isOn to the boolean value for an on switch so the program prints true.

Make sure to pick isOn, followed by true.

lessons.title: Assigning
lessons.interactiveContent:
When storing false in isOn we say that we assign a value to a variable.

Make sure to pick isOn, followed by false.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When storing false in isOn we say that we assign a value to a variable. Complete the assignment that makes the program print false.

Make sure to pick isOn, followed by false.

lessons.title: Question: Types
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are values like booleans, strings, and numbers called?

TypesVariables

Make sure to pick Types.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A program contains "Hi", 42, and true. What category describes each of these values?

TypesVariablesAssignments

Make sure to pick Types.

lessons.title: Question: Strings
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we recognize values of type string?

By the quotes " " surrounding them By the fact that they're always words or letters

By the quotes " " surrounding them .
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which detail tells you that "42" is a string, even though it looks numeric?

The quotes " " surrounding itIt is made of words or lettersIt is stored in a variable

The quotes " " surrounding it.

42"42"

42"42"true

lessons.title: Question: Booleans
lessons.interactiveContent:
What are the boolean values?

true and false"True" and "False"

true and false.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A setting must use a boolean. Which pair contains the only two boolean values?

true and false"True" and "False"1 and 0

Make sure to pick true and false.

lessons.title: Question: Assigning
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is a variable assignment?

Storing a value inside a variableGiving a variable a name

Storing a value inside a variable.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In const age = 28;, what does the assignment do?

It stores 28 in age.It gives age its name.It checks whether age equals 28.

It stores 28 in age.

lessons.title: Adding and joining
lessons.interactiveContent:
+ is the joining or adding sign. When joining two variables, we can get different results depending on their types.

Join the values and take a look at the difference between using + with strings, and with numbers.

Make sure to type +.

lessons.title: Strings and numbers 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
When joining numbers with strings, the number will be automatically transformed into a string.

Join the values and take a look at the resulting string.

Make sure to pick +.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When joining numbers with strings, the number will be automatically transformed into a string.

Join the values so the program prints the single string 1010.

Make sure to pick +.

lessons.title: Strings and numbers 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Combine a string and a number to display a player's score.

Make sure to pick 99.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Combine a string and a number so the displayed score is Your score: 99.

Make sure to pick +, followed by 99.

lessons.title: Strings and number variables
lessons.interactiveContent:
Adding a number to a string also works when we use a variable like score that stores a number, instead of a numeric value.

Make sure to pick score.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Adding a number to a string also works when we use a variable like score that stores a number, instead of a numeric value. Complete the message that prints Your score: 99.

Make sure to pick score, followed by +, and finally score.

lessons.title: Strings and booleans 1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also join strings and booleans.

Combine a string and a boolean to display a student's result. Did they pass?

Make sure to pick true.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can also join strings and booleans.

Combine the values so the student's result prints as You passed: true.

Make sure to pick +, followed by true.

lessons.title: Strings and booleans 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Again, adding a boolean to a string also works when we use a variable like pass, that stores a boolean.

Make sure to pick pass.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use + to join a string with a variable like pass that stores a boolean.

Complete the message that prints You passed: true.

Make sure to pick pass, followed by +, and finally pass.

+=

"Hi, " + namename = "Hi, "name === "Hi, "
